data.hypothesis: A 2048-source tile with the prior 256-target CTA geometry reduces source-tile iterations and synchronization rounds compared with the previously measured 1536-by-256 candidate, while retaining one thread per target and the same force arithmetic. Its 32,768 bytes of shared memory remain below the 49,152-byte limit; increased shared-memory pressure may offset the reduced loop overhead, so official timing must decide.
data.notes: The previous 1536-source-by-256-target candidate was correct and averaged 0.000999 seconds, but no per-size breakdown is provided. This is a distinct candidate; its correctness and per-size geometric-mean performance remain for the controller to evaluate. No local commands or independent measurements were used.
transformations: Cooperatively stage source x, y, z, and mass into four dynamic shared-memory arrays with a 2048-source tile (32,768 bytes).
Keep one thread per target and the existing interaction order, force expression, square root, and self-interaction exclusion.
Keep all CTA threads participating in both barriers, including inactive target-tail threads, and limit partial source tiles to valid elements.
Set block and items_per_block to 256 and request the tile's shared-memory allocation in launch.json.
